title: Rename Semio Model to Representation
description: Rename the semio-domain term "model" to "representation" across the semio/ technology, using the repo CLI `rename` command. Extend the CLI with a scope path argument so the rename can be limited to semio/ without touching other technologies (elements, coda) or historical .repo/ records. Apply the rename, verify builds/tests, and close.
summary:
Extended the repo CLI `rename` command with an optional scope argument (`rename <old> <new> [scope]`) so renames can be limited to a subfolder of the repo root. Refactored `ToolRename` to accept a scope parameter that is joined to rootDir and validated as a directory; the walk is rooted there while .gitignore/.git/node_modules skipping is preserved. Updated all existing test call sites and added `TestToolRenameScopeLimitsWalk` covering in-scope rewrite and out-of-scope preservation. All five rename tests pass (`go test -run TestApplyRenameCasings|TestToolRename`).

Rebuilt repo/cli/cli.exe and ran `repo rename model representation semio` from the repo root. Result: 94 files edited, 96 files renamed, 1 folder renamed across semio/ only. Verified semio Go (`go build ./...` clean), Rust (`cargo check --lib` only pre-existing warnings), and Python (`ast.parse`) still parse. Remaining `\bmodel\b` occurrences inside semio/ are the 8 GPL LICENSE boilerplate references ("product model", legal text) which are correct to leave. The sketchpad/react/docs content, schemas (graphql, openapi, sqlite, jsonschema, owl, xmi, rdf), asset kit JSONs, Grasshopper component metadata, .NET sources, Rhino plugin, icons folder, and Python/Go/TS implementations were all migrated.

Known follow-up (being handled in parallel by another agent, already observed in working tree): the substring-based rename over-reached in a handful of cases (IANA media types like `model/stl`, `model/gltf-binary`, `model/gltf+json`, `model/vnd.3dm`, and the phrase "data model" in semio/go/main.go header) which are not the semio domain term. Those are being reverted to their correct IANA/English meanings.
